name: Shree Ravalnath Temple
fullAddress: Shree Ravalnath Mandir, Opp. Pernem Bus Stand,  Pernem, Pernam Municipal Area, Goa 403512

Shree Jyotiba Devsthan is a famous hilltop temple near Kolhapur dedicated to Lord Jyotiba, believed to be an incarnation of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.

description: One of Pune’s most iconic and visited temples, built in the late 19th century by Dagdusheth Halwai and his wife. The temple is famous for its richly ornamented Ganesha idol and grand celebrations during Ganesh Chaturthi.

name: Sri Sri Radha Vrindavanchandra Temple

name: Shree Siddhivinayak Temple
fullAddress: SK Bole Marg, Prabhadevi, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400028, India
description:
The Shree Siddhivinayak Temple is one of the most famous and revered temples dedicated to Lord Ganesha in India.
It is located in Mumbai, specifically in the Prabhadevi area.
The temple was originally built in 1801 by Laxman Vithu and Deubai Patil.
It is known for fulfilling devotees’ wishes, which is why it is called “Siddhivinayak” (the one who grants wishes).
The idol of Lord Ganesha here is unique, with the trunk turned to the right side.
Devotees from across the country, including celebrities and politicians, visit regularly.
The temple attracts huge crowds, especially on Tuesdays and during Ganesh Chaturthi.
It is considered a powerful place for prayers related to success, prosperity, and happiness.
The temple trust also supports many charitable and social activities.
Today, it stands as a symbol of faith, devotion, and spiritual strength in Mumbai.

name: Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust, Shirdi
fullAddress: Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust Taluka Rahata, District Ahmednagar Shirdi – 423109 Maharashtra, India
description:
The Shirdi Sai Baba Temple, located in Shirdi, is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites in India, dedicated to Sai Baba of Shirdi. The temple is built around the Samadhi (resting place) of Sai Baba, where devotees come to seek blessings, peace, and spiritual guidance.

The temple complex is beautifully maintained by the Shree Saibaba Sansthan Trust and includes the Samadhi Mandir, Dwarkamai, Chavadi, and other important places associated with Sai Baba’s life. The idol of Sai Baba, made of white marble, is placed over his Samadhi and attracts millions of devotees every year.

Daily rituals such as Kakad Aarti, Madhyan Aarti, Dhoop Aarti, and Shej Aarti are performed with great devotion, creating a divine atmosphere. The temple also offers facilities like prasadalaya (free meals), accommodation, and darshan arrangements for pilgrims.

Devotees believe that Sai Baba fulfills wishes and removes difficulties, making this temple a symbol of faith, patience (Shraddha and Saburi), and unity among all religions.

name: Shri Mahalakshmi Devi Temple, Mumbai
fullAddress: Bhulabhai Desai Marg, Mahalaxmi West, Cumballa Hill, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400026, India
description:
Shri Mahalakshmi Temple is one of the most famous and sacred temples in Mumbai, dedicated to Goddess Mahalakshmi, the deity of wealth and prosperity. The temple is located near the Arabian Sea, offering a peaceful and spiritual atmosphere to devotees.

It was built in 1831 and is known for its beautiful traditional architecture, with intricate carvings and a divine sanctum. Inside the temple, three idols—Mahalakshmi, Mahakali, and Mahasaraswati—are worshipped together, representing wealth, power, and knowledge.

Thousands of devotees visit the temple daily to seek blessings for success, happiness, and financial stability. The temple becomes especially crowded during festivals like Navratri and Diwali, when it is decorated with lights and flowers.

It is believed that sincere prayers at this temple help fulfill wishes and bring prosperity into life, making it a very important Shakti Peeth for devotees.

name: Shri Tulja Bhavani Temple
fullAddress: Raje Shahaji Mahadwar Road, Jijamata Nagar, Tuljapur, Dharashiv (Osmanabad) District, Maharashtra – 413601,
description:
Shri Tulja Bhavani Temple is one of the most sacred and powerful temples in Maharashtra, located in the town of Tuljapur. The temple is dedicated to Goddess Bhavani, a fierce and protective form of Durga, worshipped as the giver of strength and courage. It is considered one of the important Shakti Peethas in India and holds deep religious significance among devotees.

The temple is believed to have been built in the 12th century and showcases traditional Hemadpanti-style architecture made of stone. The idol of Goddess Bhavani is regarded as Swayambhu (self-manifested), which increases its spiritual importance. Devotees believe that the goddess fulfills wishes and protects her followers from difficulties.

Historically, the temple is closely associated with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, who considered Tulja Bhavani as his Kuldevi (family deity). It is believed that he received a divine sword from the goddess, symbolizing power and victory.

The temple attracts lakhs of devotees throughout the year, especially during festivals like Navratri and Dussehra, when special rituals and grand celebrations are held. The temple complex also includes several smaller shrines, holy water tanks, and sacred spots that enhance the spiritual experience.

Overall, Shri Tulja Bhavani Temple is not just a place of worship but a center of faith, history, and cultural heritage, where devotees come seeking blessings for protection, success, and prosperity.

name: Shri Bhairavnath Temple

description:

Devotees believe that Bhairavnath acts as a guardian deity (Kshetrapal) who protects the village and removes negative energies. The temple is simple yet spiritually powerful, attracting devotees especially during festivals and special पूजा rituals.

fullAddress: Math Road, Budhwar Peth, Akkalkot, District Solapur, Maharashtra – 413216, India

name: Shree Vitthal Rukmini Temple
fullAddress: Main Temple Road, Pandharpur – 413304 District Solapur, Maharashtra, India
description:
Shree Vitthal Rukmini Temple in Pandharpur is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites in Maharashtra and a प्रमुख केंद्र of devotion for Lord Vitthal, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, along with Goddess Rukmini. The temple is especially vibrant during Mahashivratri, attracting devotees seeking blessings, peace, and divine connection with Lord Shiva.

name: Shri Mahalasa Narayani Temple
fullAddress: Mardol, Priol, Ponda, Goa – 403404, India
description:
Mahalasa Narayani and Mahalaxmi Devi

In ancient times, due to maritime trade and transportation, many people from Goa settled in the region of Sindhudurg. Among them, the Saraswat community was prominent. Mahalasa was chosen as the village deity of one such village, and thus the village came to be known as Mhalasa (Mhalasa).

In earlier times, Hindus lived in small settlements in this village. However, due to attacks by foreign invaders, many Hindus began migrating. With time, religious persecution increased across the Hindu population. Due to this, Saraswat people from Goa started coming here for refuge. During this period, Hindus began worshipping their deities in secrecy to protect them.

During the Portuguese rule, churches were built in the villages of Goa. The temples of the Saraswats were destroyed, and the Saraswat community began migrating to nearby regions. They brought their deities along with them and safeguarded them. In this way, many ancient deities were preserved in Sindhudurg and nearby areas.

Thus, Mahalasa Devi was established in this region by the Saraswat community. Over time, the village developed, and the temple became the center of devotion for the people. Mahalasa Devi is worshipped as a powerful and protective goddess.

From ancient times, the gods created many miraculous events related to the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan). During this event, the nectar (Amrut) emerged. To distribute this nectar among the gods, Lord Vishnu took the form of Mohini. In this enchanting form, Mohini captivated everyone and distributed the nectar among the gods.

At that time, a demon named Rahu deceitfully sat among the gods to consume the nectar. However, Lord Vishnu recognized him and severed his head. Because he had consumed the nectar, his head remained immortal. Rahu and Ketu are believed to have originated from this event.

In this way, Lord Vishnu’s Mohini avatar is worshipped as Mahalasa Devi. She is considered a manifestation of divine feminine power and is revered as a protector and benefactor of devotees.
— Shri Vasudev, Tal. Mhal, Goa
(Information based on ancient records)

The ‘Mhamal’ clan members, adopting various surnames, have migrated not only within Goa but also to Maharashtra and some other states, and have been residing there for many years. Among the Mhamal clan, surnames such as Mhamal, Mandrekar, Manjrekar, Kankonkar, Otavankar, Otavankar Naik, Naik, Aravankar Shet, Kambli, Naik, Revankar, Konkar, Varadkar, Mungekar, Khot, Tondankar, Konadkar, Varang, and many others are found. Today, it is known with joy that the original temple of their Kuladevata (family deity) for these communities is the Shri Mahalasa Temple located at Mardol, Mhalasa (Goa).

Aarti of Shri Mahalasa Devi

Victory to the Goddess, victory to the Goddess, victory to Mahalasa Mother.
Moon-like radiant, bearer of life, O divine one. ॥

During the churning of the ocean, the nectar emerged.
For its consumption, the gods and demons gathered.
The gods became anxious at that moment.
In that time of crisis, Lord Vishnu took refuge (in you). ॥1॥ Victory to the Goddess....

Beautiful and graceful, filled with divine charm.
Her beauty enchants the minds of devotees.
Holding the pot of nectar in her hands.
Even Rahu and Ketu were captivated. ॥2॥ Victory to the Goddess....

Such a feminine form, Shri Hari became Mahalasa.
Countless gods were fascinated by her form.
Day and night, Mahalasa Mother is worshipped.
In times of distress, she grants happiness and peace. ॥3॥ Victory to the Goddess....

name: Shri Nageshi Temple
fullAddress: Bandiwade, Donshiwado, Bandora, Ponda, Goa – 403401, India
description:
Shri Nageshi Temple is one of the oldest and most sacred temples in Goa, located in the serene village of Bandora near Ponda. Dedicated to Lord Shiva in the form of Nagesh, the temple is believed to house a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shivling, making it highly revered among devotees.

The temple dates back to around the 14th century and has historical significance linked to the Vijayanagara Empire. Unlike many temples in Goa, it remained at its original location and was preserved through centuries.

The temple complex features a beautiful दीपस्तंभ (lamp tower), a sacred water tank, and intricate wooden carvings depicting scenes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata. The peaceful surroundings and spiritual ambiance attract devotees and tourists seeking divine blessings and tranquility.

name: Shri Ramnath Devasthan
fullAddress: Ramnathim, Ponda, Bandiwada, Goa 403401
description:
Shri Ramnath Devasthan is one of the most revered temples in Goa, located in the peaceful village of Bandora near Ponda. The temple is dedicated to Lord Ramnath, a divine form symbolizing the unity of Lord Vishnu (Hari) and Lord Shiva (Hara), making it spiritually significant for devotees.

The temple has deep historical roots and is closely associated with the legend of Lord Rama, who is believed to have installed a Shivling to seek redemption after the battle with Ravana.

Originally located in Loutolim, the deity was moved to Bandora during the Portuguese period for protection. The temple follows the Panchayatan tradition and houses other deities such as Shanteri, Kamakshi, Laxmi Narayan, and Ganapati.

With its beautiful architecture, peaceful surroundings, and vibrant festivals like Mahashivratri and Jatra, the temple attracts thousands of devotees seeking blessings, spiritual peace, and cultural experience.

name: Shri Saptakoteshwar Temple
fullAddress: Deulwada, Narve, Bicholim, Goa – 403504, India
description:
Shri Saptakoteshwar Temple is one of the most ancient and revered Shiva temples in Goa, located in the serene village of Narva. It dates back to the Kadamba dynasty and was once the royal deity of the Kadamba kings, making it historically significant in the Konkan region.

The temple has witnessed multiple destructions and restorations over centuries, and was finally rebuilt under the orders of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in the 17th century.

Surrounded by lush greenery and peaceful surroundings, the temple showcases a blend of traditional Hindu and Indo-Portuguese architectural styles, featuring a दीपस्तंभ (lamp tower), mandap, and sacred tank (Panchaganga Tirtha).

It is considered one of the six important Shiva temples in the Konkan region and attracts devotees seeking spiritual peace, blessings, and historical connection.

name: Shri Mahalaxmi Temple, Panaji
fullAddress: Dr Dada Vaidya Rd, next to Mushtifund, Situated, Saunthan, Panaji, Goa 403001, India
description:
Shri Mahalaxmi Temple is one of the most important and sacred temples in Goa, located in the heart of Panaji city. Dedicated to Goddess Mahalaxmi, the temple is considered the presiding deity of Panaji and attracts devotees from all communities.

Built in 1818, it holds historical significance as one of the first Hindu temples allowed to be constructed in Goa during Portuguese rule. The temple has a rich past, where the deity was carefully moved across locations to protect it from destruction before finally being स्थापित in Panaji.

The temple showcases traditional Goan architecture with a peaceful ambiance, intricate interiors, and a beautifully adorned idol of the goddess. Major festivals like Navratri and Maruti Jatra are celebrated with great devotion, attracting thousands of visitors every year.

name: Shri Maruti Temple, Panaji
fullAddress: Altinho Hill, Mala, Panaji, Goa – 403001, India
description:
Shri Maruti Temple is a well-known and vibrant temple located on Altinho Hill in Panaji, offering a scenic view of the city. Dedicated to Lord Hanuman, the temple is easily recognizable by its bright orange-colored idol and striking architecture.

The temple holds great spiritual importance among locals and is especially crowded on Tuesdays and Saturdays, which are considered auspicious for Lord Hanuman. Devotees visit to seek strength, courage, and protection from negative energies.

Its elevated location and peaceful surroundings make it not only a place of worship but also a popular spot for visitors looking to experience both devotion and panoramic views of Panaji.

name: Shree Somnath Temple
fullAddress: Prabhas Patan, Somnath, Gir Somnath District, Gujarat – 362268, India
description:
Shree Somnath Temple is one of the most sacred and ancient temples of Lord Shiva, located on the western coast of Gujarat near the Arabian Sea. It is the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas, making it a highly significant pilgrimage site for Hindus.

The temple has a rich history of destruction and reconstruction, symbolizing resilience and faith. It is believed to have been rebuilt several times, with the current structure completed in 1951 under the guidance of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Built in the Chalukya style of architecture, the temple stands majestically by the sea, offering a spiritually uplifting atmosphere. The continuous sound of waves and the divine ambiance make it a powerful place for devotion and inner peace.

Thousands of devotees visit daily to seek blessings, especially during festivals like Mahashivratri and Kartik Purnima.

name: Shri Brahmadev Ji Temple
fullAddress: Brahma-Karmali, Nagargao Village, Sattari Taluka, North Goa – 403506, India
description:
Shri Brahmadev Ji Temple is one of the rare temples in India dedicated to Lord Brahma, the creator in the Hindu Trinity. Located in the quiet village of Brahma-Karmali in Sattari, Goa, the temple holds immense historical and spiritual importance.

The temple houses a unique 12th-century idol carved from black basalt stone during the Kadamba period. The idol depicts Lord Brahma with a beard in Trimurti form, symbolizing Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh.

Surrounded by dense greenery and serene natural surroundings, the temple offers a peaceful spiritual experience. It is believed that the idol was moved here centuries ago to protect it during invasions, adding to its historical significance.

This temple is considered one of the very few Brahma temples in India, making it a unique pilgrimage destination for devotees and history enthusiasts alike.

name: Shree Kamakshi Temple
fullAddress: Thal, Shiroda, Ponda Taluka, South Goa – 403103, India
description:
Shri Kamakshi Temple is one of the most important and revered temples in Goa, located amidst the scenic hills of Shiroda village. The temple was built in the late 16th century and is dedicated to Goddess Kamakshi, a powerful form of Shakti symbolizing strength, compassion, and protection.

Originally, the deity was worshipped in Raia, but during the Portuguese period, the idol was safely moved to Shiroda to preserve it from destruction. The temple features traditional Goan architecture with a grand Mahadwar (entrance gate), a tall दीपस्तंभ (lamp tower), and a serene temple tank.

The temple complex also houses other deities like Shantadurga, Lakshmi Narayan, and Rayeshwar, making it a spiritually rich destination. Major festivals like Navratri, Jatra, and Amavasya palanquin processions attract thousands of devotees seeking blessings and peace.

name: Shri Chandreshwar Bhootnath Temple
fullAddress: Chandranath Hill, Paroda Village, Quepem Taluka, South Goa – 403705, India
description:
Shri Chandreshwar Bhootnath Temple is one of the oldest and most historically significant temples in Goa, located atop the scenic Chandranath Hill in South Goa. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva in the form of Chandreshwar, meaning “Lord of the Moon,” along with Bhootnath, another powerful form of Shiva.

The temple is believed to be over 2000 years old and is associated with the Bhoja dynasty, who once ruled this region and considered Lord Chandreshwar their patron deity.

A unique feature of the temple is its sacred Shivling, which is positioned in such a way that moonlight falls directly on it during full moon nights. It is believed that water droplets appear on the Shivling when touched by moon rays, adding to its mystical significance.

Surrounded by dense greenery and offering panoramic views from the hilltop, the temple provides a peaceful and spiritual atmosphere. Major festivals like Mahashivratri, Hanuman Jayanti, and Dussehra are celebrated with great devotion, attracting many devotees.

name: Shri Vijayadurga Temple
fullAddress: Keri, Betki, Ponda, Goa – 403404, India
description:
Shri Vijayadurga Temple is a sacred and historically significant temple located in the serene village of Keri in Ponda, Goa. Dedicated to Goddess Vijayadurga, a powerful form of Durga, the temple is deeply revered as a Kuldevi by many Goan families.

The temple dates back to around 1560 and was relocated from Sancoale during the Portuguese period to protect the deity. It showcases beautiful traditional Goan temple architecture, including a grand mandap, deepastambha (lamp tower), and intricate Kaavi art on the walls.

Surrounded by lush greenery and peaceful natural surroundings, the temple offers a calm and spiritual atmosphere. Festivals like Navratri and Jatra are celebrated with great devotion, attracting devotees from across Goa and beyond.

name: Shri Navadurga Temple

name: Shri Kopeshwar Temple
fullAddress: Shri Kopeshwar Temple, Khidrapur Village, Shirol Taluka, Kolhapur District, Maharashtra – 416108, India
description:
Shri Kopeshwar Temple is an ancient and architecturally magnificent temple located in Khidrapur on the banks of the Krishna River in Maharashtra. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva, worshipped here as “Kopeshwar,” meaning the wrathful or angry form of the deity.

The temple dates back to the 11th–12th century and was built by the Shilahara king Gandaraditya, making it one of the oldest temples in the region.

One of the most unique features of this temple is that it houses both Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu (Dhopeshwar), which is very rare in Indian temples.

The temple is famous for its extraordinary stone architecture and intricate carvings depicting gods, dancers, and mythological scenes. It is often referred to as the “Khajuraho of Maharashtra” due to its artistic beauty.

The structure of the temple is divided into four main parts—Swargamandap, Sabhamandap, Antaral, and Garbhagriha. The Swargamandap is especially unique with an open circular ceiling that allows sunlight to enter, creating a divine ambiance.

Interestingly, unlike most Shiva temples, there is no Nandi idol directly facing the Shiva Lingam inside the sanctum, which makes it architecturally distinctive.

The temple has inscriptions and historical records that reflect the cultural and political history of the region, including battles and royal patronage.

Mahashivratri is the major festival celebrated here, attracting a large number of devotees and tourists.

Surrounded by natural beauty and located near the Maharashtra–Karnataka border, the temple offers a peaceful and spiritually enriching experience.

Daily rituals include Kakad Aarti, Paduka Pooja, Rudrabhishek, Maha Aarti, and Palkhi procession, which are performed with great devotion throughout the day.

The temple surroundings are very peaceful, with riverbanks, Audumbar trees, and natural beauty, making it ideal for spiritual experience and meditation.

It is one of the most important Datta Sampradaya pilgrimage centers in India, along with places like Ganagapur and Girnar.
